record.tranche_reason: Chapter 4 directly compares training with data augmentation alone against training with data augmentation plus weight decay and dropout, using the same intervention described in V6. The thesis identifies this chapter as extending the relevant Hernández-García and König publications.
record.gate_note: Chapter 4 reports its own comparisons. Individual values in Figures 4.3–4.9 are not reconstructed from plots; rows use the text and flattened summary tables. Results cited from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Chapter 4 directly tests V6's augmented-image-classifier comparison by removing weight decay and dropout together and measuring held-out accuracy. It extends publications including the V6 original arXiv:1802.07042; overlapping results should not be counted as independent replication.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that augmentation alone often matches or improves accuracy relative to augmentation plus weight decay and dropout, and adapts better to data and depth changes with inherited hyperparameters. They acknowledge that suitably retuned explicit regularization may still provide a final performance boost.
record.recipe_differences: The thesis reports a chapter extending the Hernández-García and König data-augmentation-versus-explicit-regularization publications. It compares bundled weight decay and dropout against augmentation-only training across architectures, data sets, and reduced-data or changed-depth settings; dropout's effect is not isolated.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparison changes with augmentation scheme, amount of training data, architecture depth, and data set. The text says heavier augmentation improved CIFAR performance over light augmentation, but not ImageNet.

fits_no_version.finding: Reduced-data and changed-depth experiments show better retention of each model's own original accuracy after joint removal of explicit regularizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: With inherited hyperparameters, augmentation-only training can retain a larger fraction of its original accuracy when training data or architecture depth changes.

record.peer_reviewed: PhD thesis, Institute of Cognitive Science, University of Osnabrück
record.problems: Weight decay and dropout are varied together, preventing attribution to dropout alone. The study uses original hyperparameters rather than retuning them for each condition; the authors note the heavier augmentation scheme was not optimized. Some condition-specific results appear only in figures and are not extracted here.
record.rows_left_out: Individual condition-specific performance values in Figures 4.3–4.4 and 4.6–4.9 are not transcribed because the supplied text does not state their exact values. Figure 4.5 training dynamics are not test-error comparisons.

untested.parts: No own random-label versus natural-label training experiment.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to interpolate; changing depth does not test this.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.

Dropout's isolated contribution, fully connected classifiers, a dropout-rate sweep demonstrating underfitting, and the original very-small-training-set regime are untested. Reduced-data and changed-depth conditions retain the original regularization hyperparameters without retuning.
No magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness or ranking of generalization gaps.
No removal of examples selected by memorization influence.

missing.what: Direct All-CNN/CIFAR-10 light-augmentation accuracies with versus without weight decay and dropout: original depth approximately 92 versus 93.3%, deeper approximately 85 versus 93.4%, and shallower approximately 82 versus 90%. These stated values permit direct comparisons that the normalized aggregate R8 does not.

record.verdict_notes: The thesis is not itself a listed original source, so verdicts are supplied, but Chapter 4 explicitly extends the listed V6 original and related publications. Aggregate superiority does not establish superiority in every model condition. Reduced-data retention ratios should not be used as direct accuracy comparisons. Chapters 5–8 do not test additional listed versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not tested.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks.
No comparison of adaptive and SGD optimizers.

Dropout is bundled with weight decay, so their separate effects are not identified. The study does not test the claim about very small training sets or the cited Hernández-García and König 2018 removal comparison as a separate experiment.
